key_insight: UFO-4D reconstructs dense, time-varying 3D scenes from just two unposed images in a single feedforward pass by directly predicting dynamic 3D Gaussian splats and camera poses, removing the need for slow test-time optimization.
problem_solved: Enables fast, unified dense 4D reconstruction (geometry + motion + camera pose) from only two unposed images, addressing fragmentation and slow optimization in prior methods.
method: Feedforward network that predicts dynamic 3D Gaussian splats representing per-point appearance, geometry, and motion from two unposed images.
Jointly estimates camera poses and time-varying 3D structure to ensure consistent geometry and motion across views.
Trained with differentiable splatting / rendering and multi-view / temporal consistency losses to produce explicit, test-time-ready 4D outputs without optimization.
impact: Delivers real-time-capable, unified 4D reconstruction from minimal input, making fast scene capture, view synthesis, and motion analysis practical for downstream AI/ML applications like AR/VR, robotics, and content creation.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: two unposed input images → feedforward network → estimated poses + dynamic 3D Gaussian splats → rendered temporal sequence / novel views
Illustration of 3D Gaussian splats with motion vectors showing dynamic deformation across time
Comparison bar chart: inference time vs. optimization-based baselines (UFO-4D much faster)
Qualitative before/after panels: input images, reconstructed geometry, and synthesized intermediate frames
paper_title: UFO-4D: Unposed Feedforward 4D Reconstruction from Two Images
paper_authors: Junhwa Hur, Charles Herrmann, Songyou Peng, Philipp Henzler, Zeyu Ma
